FXUS66 KSTO 272045
AFDSTO

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Sacramento CA
1245 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

For additional details on weather and expected impacts over the
next 7 days, please visit weather.gov/sto/briefing.

.KEY MESSAGES... 

 - Dry, seasonable weather with Valley and Delta fog chances into
   Saturday
 
 - Flood Advisory in effect through 8 PM Saturday for coastal 
   flooding and erosion potential for the Delta vicinity
 
 - Active pattern expected to return late weekend into mid-week,
   with periods of precipitation, breezy winds, and thunderstorm 
   chances

 - Breezy to gusty north to east winds develop Tuesday and
   Wednesday

&&

.DISCUSSION...

...Today-Saturday... 
Ridging over the region will continue to promote drier weather 
and warming temperatures through Saturday. The main weather
concern will be the potential for dense fog development across 
portions of the central and southern Sacramento Valley, the Delta,
and the northern San Joaquin Valley tonight into Saturday 
morning. Daytime high temperatures in the upper 50s to 60s are 
forecast for the Valleys/Foothills and 40s to 50s for the 
mountains through Saturday. 

King Tides will continue today resulting in water levels up to 
1.5 feet above normal. Minor impacts from coastal flooding and 
erosion are anticipated for low- lying areas throughout the Delta 
and vicinity. A Flood Advisory remains in effect until 8 pm 
Saturday for coastal flooding.

...Sunday-Wednesday... 
Confidence continues to increase in a wet, and unsettled weather 
pattern Sunday through mid next week as a series of systems move 
across the area. The first weather system is expected to bring 
widespread precipitation, light mountain snow above 7500 feet, 
gusty southerly winds, and isolated thunderstorm chances Sunday 
into Monday. The heaviest precipitation is expected Sunday
afternoon into the overnight hours. Precipitation totals of 0.25 
to around 0.60 inches are forecast for the Sacramento Valley 
(locally up to 1" in the northern Sacramento Valley), with 0.25 
inches or less in the Delta and northern San Joaquin Valley. Up to
0.75-2.25" are possible in the foothills and mountains. Snow 
levels will rise above 7500-8000 feet, with 1 to 4 inches of snow 
generally south of Highway 50, with up to 6 inches over the higher
peaks. Minor travel delays and slippery roads will be possible at
pass level. Breezy to gusty southerly winds are also expected 
with this system. Gusts of 20 to 35 mph are expected in the lower 
elevations, with gusts of 40 to 55 mph over the Sierra crest. 
Isolated thunderstorm chances are possible Sunday afternoon into 
Monday. Main storm hazards include dangerous lighting, small 
hail, gusty winds and brief heavy rain. In addition, latest CAMs
suggest the potential for a Shasta Convergence zone developing 
Sunday night, which may bring locally heavy rain.

Another system arrives late Monday night/Tuesday, but ensembles 
continue to trend farther south with the track of the system. At 
this point, generally light precipitation and mountain snow above
6500 feet are expected. 

Breezy to gusty north to east winds develop Tuesday into
Wednesday. The strongest winds expected along the west side of 
the Valley, Delta and Sierra, with a 40-70% chance of wind gusts 
exceeding 35 mph. Otherwise, dry weather is expected on Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION...

Lingering IFR/LIFR conditions this morning due to Valley fog.
Visibilities should improve by the afternoon as fog begins to
lift, leading to mainly VFR conditions with light surface winds
through around 04z Saturday. BR/FG will again develop in the
Sacramento Valley, northern San Joaquin Valley, and Delta around
05-09z Saturday bringing periods of MVFR/IFR/LIFR conditions
through Saturday morning. Probabilities of visibilities less than
1/2SM are around 40-60% for Saturday morning. 

&&

.STO WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&
